messages:
maria_support: Heads-up — just got an escalated ticket (tenant id t-83ff) where tool calls are returning schema validation errors even though the payload matches the expected schema. Customer reports this started after a recent alias rename.

maria_support: Repro notes from customer: POST /v1/tools/call with {
  "tool": "payment.charge",
  "args": {"amount":1000, "currency":"USD"}
} returns 400 schema_error with message "unexpected field \"amount\" for tool id \"tool_4c3\""

maria_support: They say the tool used to be named "payments.charge" (plural) and was renamed to "payment.charge" (singular) last week. On our logs the incoming request shows the tool name as the singular form, but the registry returned tool_4c3 which is the OLD UUID (payments.charge).

maria_support: Quick log snippet (redacted):
```
req id=rc-92fa tenant=t-83ff tool="payment.charge" auth=ok
registry.resolve -> alias_match: payments.charge -> tool_4c3 (scope=tenant:t-83ff)
serve.call -> selected=tool_4c3 schema=payments.v1
validation.error -> missing required field \"amount_cents\"
```

jia_engineer: Hmm. Sounds like alias resolution returned a tenant-scoped legacy mapping. Did the customer have a tenant-level alias override?

maria_support: They said they didn't manage aliases manually. They never saw the plural form in their UI. Only noticed by error and logs.

ashley_prodops: registry-bot shows a backfill job last Tuesday that attempted to migrate alias names across tenants — could be a partial failure for t-83ff. Passing to registry team. @registry-bot can you paste the job status?

registry-bot: backfill/alias-normalize-2026-03-10 status=partial_fail tenants_failed=[t-83ff, t-91aa] error=conflict-on-rename

jia_engineer: If a tenant-level alias existed with the old name, rename backfills may have created a shadow alias that still points to the old uuid. Need to check alias table ordering: tenant-scoped should win over global, but rename might've left both.

maria_support: Customer provided request id rc-92fa and example call. Can someone repro on staging with t-83ff data snapshot? Priority = P1 for them (billing pipeline blocked).

sre_john: I'll spin up a staging replay using the snapshot. Quick check: can you DM me the snapshot link and the exact curl?

maria_support: Sent. curl example:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tools/call \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer <token-for-t-83ff>" \
 -H "X-Tenant-ID: t-83ff" \
 -d '{"tool":"payment.charge","args":{"amount":10.00,"currency":"USD"}}'
```

maria_support: Note: the customer is using amount as float dollars — our schema expects amount_cents int, but that was validated against payments.v1 schema until last week — they say we previously accepted the float because the old tool wrapper handled conversion. The escaped old uuid suggests the wrong tool impl is being selected.

jia_engineer: Two likely vectors: 1) alias mapping still resolving to old UUID due to tenant-scoped override, 2) tool version compatibility fallback returning a legacy implementation when a model variant isn't available. Check registry cache TTL too.

sre_john: Reproduced on staging: when I replay with X-Tenant-ID t-83ff we resolve to tool_4c3. When I remove the header or use a different tenant it resolves to tool_e9b (the new singular UUID). So tenant-scoped alias is shadowing.

sre_john: Dump of alias rows for t-83ff:
```
alias_name: payment.charge scope=tenant:t-83ff -> tool_uuid=tool_e9b (created 2026-02-28)
alias_name: payments.charge scope=tenant:t-83ff -> tool_uuid=tool_4c3 (created 2025-08-05)
```

sre_john: Uh — so both exist. Global alias mapping was changed, but tenant still had older plural alias left behind. Our resolver is doing case-insensitive match + exact match and picking the first matching alias in the tenant scope. Because their request uses singular, I'm not sure why payments.charge matched — need to see normalizer behavior.

jia_engineer: Could be our casefold/whitespace normalizer bug: we normalize dots and plural endings when building lookup keys for tenants, and an earlier migration normalized both aliases to the same key, causing the older alias to shadow the new one in the tenant index.

ashley_prodops: For an immediate mitigation, we could add a safe fallback in the runtime: if selected tool's schema doesn't match the request shape but a same-name alias exists with a different uuid, try resolving again ignoring tenant-level aliases. But that's risky for isolation.

maria_support: Customer needs a fix now — billing is blocked. Any non-risky short-term action?

jia_engineer: Short-term: remove the tenant-scoped payments.charge alias (tool_4c3) for t-83ff after confirming with team. That will let global/new alias resolve. We should also mark the tenant for re-run of the backfill.

ashley_prodops: I'll coordinate with security and product to confirm removal. @registry-bot open a ticket and mark as hotfix.

registry-bot: ticket created REG-4219 summary="remove tenant alias payments.charge for t-83ff" severity=high

sre_john: After removing the alias the customer's call resolves to tool_e9b and validation passes (I replayed their exact body).

maria_support: Customer notified and unblocked. They asked for root cause explanation so we need a postmortem note: backfill left duplicate/normalized keys and tenant-level shadow alias remained.

jia_engineer: I'll write a short postmortem and propose guardrails: (1) backfill should atomically migrate tenant aliases or fail, (2) add a registry consistency check that flags duplicate normalized keys per tenant, (3) add a runtime safety check that logs when schema mismatch + alternate alias exists for same normalized key.

maria_support: Thanks all. Please paste the final ladder of actions and the postmortem link here when done so I can close the customer's escalation. :thumbsup:

jia_engineer: Will do — PR for the registry migration guardrail in review, postmortem draft at https://internal.redwood.ai/pm/REG-4219/pm-draft (will update).
